evidence.mission_note: A manual 3.0i Z3 roadster in the ideal budget band is squarely the primary enthusiast-bridge target. Fit hinges on documenting the cooling work and the rear structure before money moves.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2001 Z3 3.0i roadster with a factory 5-speed manual, Topaz Blue over tan, Premium and Sport packages, 76,750 claimed miles and a claimed clean Carfax, at $11,000 OBO. The photos support the colour, manual shifter, BBS-type wheels and a fresh-looking top. The seller discloses faded rear bumper and trunk paint, a cracked fog light, a small door dent, rim scrapes and a 2021 check-engine light that was reset with no stated code. Photos also show a worn steering-wheel rim and hazy headlights. The most important model-specific claim, a Feb 2026 water pump, thermostat and upper-hose job, is seller prose only. The radiator and expansion tank go unmentioned. Rear subframe and trunk-floor condition is entirely unaddressed. There is no VIN, so identity and history cannot yet be checked. Price sits at the low end of the $10,905–$13,895 fair range.
evidence.next_action: Email the seller for the VIN, the Feb 2026 cooling and Jan 2026 top invoices, and trunk-floor and underside photos, and ask whether a PPI at an Albuquerque BMW independent can happen before any deposit.
